Mobile · iOS · Evidence review

Make agent progress visible. Keep the booking decision human.

A focused review of chat assistants, travel cards and shopping actions for a hotel agent that can search and prepare—but must hand the final reservation to the traveller.

01 / DECIDE

The interface should carry the state.

Keep the traveller chat as the front door. Let one durable activity card explain a long task, make real options easy to compare, and put the full booking terms in view before asking for agreement.

01 · WORK

One task card, few chat interruptions

Use a short “Thinking” cue for a brief wait. For a multi-step search, show the current action and a small, expandable activity record in place. Keep status updates out of the message stream. ChatGPT sequence ↗

02 · COMPARE

Show options as a readable list

Keep two or more alternatives scannable without requiring a sideways swipe. Put room, dates, guest fit, cancellation and full total on each candidate. Offer “edit search” in the chat. Expedia cards ↗

03 · AGREE

Agreement is its own checkpoint

Show one complete, versioned quote before “Agree to these terms.” Agreement records permission to proceed; it does not submit the hotel reservation. Architecture ↗

04 · VERIFY

Name who acts, then verify

Tell the traveller when the hotel checkout is theirs. After their explicit “Check booking” request, distinguish confirmed from unresolved. Never turn a spinner, payment message or timeout into “booked.” Expedia pending state ↗

Keep the agreed boundary: the traveller performs the final reservation submission. Halcy’s chat agreement is not proof of a reservation, and stopping assistance does not cancel a hotel booking. See the architecture decisions.

02 / ACTIVITY

Long work needs a legible beginning, middle and end.

ChatGPT’s Deep Research flow is the clearest task-level precedent in this sample. Its stills move from a proposed plan, through an in-progress card, to an explicit stopped state or a report. The cards remain attached to the conversation.

The images are ordered screens from Mobbin, not frames from a continuous recording. They establish the visible states and controls, not animation timing or what happened between captures.

Brief wait versus active generation

Grok · a timed “Thinking” label

“Thinking · 2s” is a compact cue for a short response wait. By itself it would not explain a hotel search, a retry, or a user-owned checkout.

Grok · stop while generating

A clear stop control is available during generation. The same label must not imply that a reservation or payment was cancelled.

Claude · generation indicator and stop

This is reply-level activity: a small indicator and a square stop button by the composer. The inspected regeneration flow does not show a durable multi-step task record.

Open source flow ↗

Do not expose “Thoughts” as workflow evidence. Grok’s sampled response flow includes an expandable Thoughts label, but that is not a verified booking action. For Halcy, disclose observable work—such as “Checking room availability”—and preserve hidden reasoning.

03 / CHOOSE

Good cards answer “what, when, how much—and who pays?”

Travel and commerce screens are useful for their information hierarchy, not their authority model. Their “Select,” “Reserve” and checkout actions must not be copied as Halcy approval language.

Booking.com · the early property summary

Dates, three adults, the two-night price and a next action are visible together. “You won’t be charged yet” answers only the immediate payment question: the screenshot does not show the eventual amount, recipient, tax treatment or cancellation deadline at this point.

Booking.com · iOS · Mobbin flow, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Open property-detail flow ↗

Booking.com · room terms beside the total

The offer puts occupancy, room layout, amenities, non-refundable status, “Pay online,” discount and the two-night total in one card. “We have 1 left” adds urgency; availability and price still need revalidation before Halcy presents a quote.

Booking.com · iOS · Mobbin “Price information” flow, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Open price-information flow ↗

Airbnb · itemized price disclosure

Dates and guest count anchor the breakdown. Nightly price, discount and service fee roll into a visible guest total. In this capture there is no tax line; the separate listing flow labels a price “before taxes.” Keep the full mandatory total visible at Halcy’s agreement point.

Airbnb · iOS · Mobbin flow, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Open price-breakdown flow ↗ · Listing-detail flow ↗

Expedia · vertical alternatives with totals

Two property cards stack vertically, with the search dates and occupancy retained above them. Each card shows total including taxes and fees and the per-night equivalent. Rewards and scarcity cues compete for attention; Halcy should order by the traveller’s stated criteria, not urgency.

Expedia · iOS · Mobbin “Searching for a stay” flow, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Open search flow ↗

Amazon Rufus · an actionable recommendation in chat

The recommendation lives inside the assistant conversation and carries enough product context to act on: name, rating, price and a route to more offers. The linked Add to Cart flow labels “Add to Cart” and “Buy Now” separately and acknowledges an add with a toast. For Halcy, likewise separate a comparison/save action from agreeing to terms and the hotel’s final submit.

Amazon Shopping · iOS · Mobbin flows, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Rufus chat ↗ · Add-to-cart sequence ↗

Expedia · pending is not confirmed

The checkout says confirmation is still being checked and asks the traveller not to refresh or go back. The Mobbin flow ends on this pending screen; it does not supply evidence of a final confirmed reservation. Halcy should preserve that distinction and never retry a payment or booking blindly.

Expedia · iOS · Mobbin “Book a hotel” flow, inspected 05 Oct 2026
Open booking flow ↗

Layout choice: Expedia’s stacked results keep several totals in view; Booking.com’s room offer reveals a neighboring rate at the edge of a horizontally moving set. Prefer a vertical list as the default for real alternatives, and keep every option reachable without relying on a carousel. Expand details only when the mandatory terms remain easy to find before agreement.

05 / MAP

Map the screen to the coordinator state.

Use the architecture’s explicit state and control owner as the source of truth. Cards and chat copy should reflect that record—not become a second, conversational state machine.

Clarifying

Keep it conversational

Message: “I have 12–16 June 2027. How many adults, and is free cancellation important?” Ask only for a missing requirement.

Action / next: Reply in chat or edit the request. Do not show an empty progress spinner while waiting for an answer.

Searching

Compact task row

Message: “Checking rooms for 12–16 June 2027 · 2 adults.” Expand for completed observable steps, such as dates set or room availability checked.

Action / next: Stop search or edit dates/guests in place. Keep the conversation anchored; do not force-scroll as activity changes. Use counts or elapsed time only when they are measured facts. A bounded automatic retry is appropriate only for a safe read-only lookup, never for checkout submission or payment.

Search interrupted / no match

Explain the recovery path

Message: “The hotel search timed out before I could compare rooms,” or “No room matched your dates and two-adult requirement.” State what is known and what failed.

Action / next: Offer “Retry search,” “Edit dates or guests,” and “Stop.” A no-match result should suggest which soft preference to relax; do not silently weaken a hard requirement or claim every room is unavailable.

Preparing

Activity card plus return path

Message: “Comparing the cancellation terms and full totals.” Keep the card attached to the run so the traveller can return after switching apps.

Action / next: Stop assistance or edit the search. “Stop” stops the agent’s work; it does not cancel a hotel reservation.

Awaiting agreement

Pin the complete quote

Show before the CTA: hotel, room/rate, absolute dates, occupancy, inclusions, cancellation deadline and penalties, full total/currency including mandatory taxes, amount payable now and later, guarantee obligations, and payment recipient.

Action / next: “Agree to these terms” or “Change search.” Bind consent to this exact quote version. A changed price, room or term invalidates the old agreement.

Traveller control

Say who owns checkout

Message: “The hotel checkout is open in the booking window. Complete the final reservation there; Halcy is not reading the private payment form. Return here when you’re done.”

Action / next: Traveller completes the final submission. Halcy makes no observations, screenshots or browser actions while the traveller owns the sensitive form.

Verifying

Restricted check, honest wait

Message: “Checking for a hotel confirmation.” Keep the pending state distinct from payment success or a changed URL.

Action / next: Only after the traveller taps “Check booking,” inspect safe hotel-visible evidence. No auto-refresh of payment, duplicate submit or replacement booking.

Unavailable / repriced

Keep history, disable stale action

Message: “That room is no longer available at £824. I’ve kept the old quote for reference; its agreement button is disabled.”

Action / next: Revalidate eligible alternatives, let the traveller edit criteria, and show a fresh complete quote before a new agreement.

Hold expired

Do not renew silently

Message: “The hotel’s hold has expired. This room and price are no longer reserved.”

Action / next: Recheck current availability and terms, then request fresh agreement. Never imply the expired hold persists or renew it without the traveller.

Traveller returns

Restore context, preserve ownership

Message: “Your hotel checkout is still the next step. The last safe status is ‘waiting for you.’”

Action / next: Return to the same checkout window or explicitly tap “Check booking.” Do not infer abandonment, cancellation or submission from app backgrounding.

Verified failure

Offer only safe recovery

Message: “The hotel says it could not complete this reservation.” Show the hotel’s safe, relevant reason when available; do not ask for card numbers or bank codes.

Action / next: Keep the traveller in control of another payment method. Search for a replacement only when the original attempt is resolved.

Outcome unknown

No blind retry

Message: “I can’t verify whether the hotel accepted the reservation. Keep the booking window open; don’t submit again while we check.”

Action / next: Safe “Check booking” or return to the hotel window. No “Retry payment” or automatic replacement until the original outcome is resolved.

Confirmed / stopped

Use separate words

Confirmed: Show the hotel reference and stay details only when safe hotel evidence matches the approved quote. Attribute traveller-reported completion as reported.

Stopped: “Halcy stopped checking. Your reservation was not cancelled by this action.” Stopping help and cancelling a reservation are separate actions.

Make the next actor clear

Your hotel checkout is open in the booking window.

05 · CHECK

Resolve, or say it is unknown

Checking hotel confirmationLooking for a safe confirmation reference.
Confirmed

Still unknown

Changed / unavailable: disable the old quote, preserve it as history, and request fresh agreement for any replacement.

The sample price math is intentionally consistent for illustration only. Production copy must be populated from the verified, versioned quote and its evidence.

07 / LIMITS

Evidence gaps & the next useful tests

This is a reference review, not a usability study or a claim that any competitor has the safest booking flow.

Mobbin archive limits

All examples are iOS captures opened through Mobbin on 05 Oct 2026. The plugin did not expose source-app version or screenshot capture date, and its flow data contained stills rather than playable animations. Observed order is supportable; transition timing, easing, refresh behavior and unshown outcomes are not.

Handoff is the largest gap

The sampled assistant flows do not show a hotel-style private browser handoff, user-return state or restricted verification. Expedia provides a checkout-pending screen, but the selected flow ends before an independently verified result. Halcy’s rules come from its architecture, not competitor convention.

Focused usability questions

Can travellers compare room total, cancellation and payee without opening every card? Do they understand that agreement is not a reservation? After backgrounding, can they tell whether they, Halcy or the hotel is acting? Does “unknown—do not submit again” prevent a duplicate attempt? Test large text, screen-reader labels, keyboard overlap, reduced motion and 44px targets. Group approval remains future scope; the MVP has one traveller who approves and submits.
